questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

"They decided to B. split the winnings C. between the four D. members of the group."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The grammatical issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "**between**."
 
• The preposition "**between**" is used when referring to two entities, while "**among**" is used for more than two.
 
• Since the sentence refers to "**the four members of the group**," the correct preposition to use is "**among**."
 
• Therefore, the phrase "**between the four**" should be corrected to "**among the four**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They decided to split the winnings **among the four** members of the group."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "They decided to"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "split the winnings"** – This part of the sentence is also correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "members of the group"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

"A. The new smartphone is B. much more sleeker C. and lighter than D. the previous model."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the phrase "**much more sleeker**."
 
• The word "**sleeker**" is the comparative form of the adjective "sleek," and it should not be preceded by "**much more**."
 
• Using both "**much more**" and the comparative form "**sleeker**" together is redundant and grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should simply be "**much sleeker**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new smartphone is much sleeker and lighter than the previous model."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The new smartphone is"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "and lighter than"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "the previous model."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:**

He will be promoted ________ he improves his communication and leadership skills.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**3**' i.e. **provided that**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The conjunction "**provided that**" is used to indicate a condition that must be met for a certain outcome to occur.
 
• The sentence mentions a condition for promotion, making "**provided that**" the most appropriate choice.
 
• "**Unless**" (Option 1) is incorrect as it implies a negative condition, which does not fit the context here.
 
• "**Although**" (Option 2) is incorrect as it is used to indicate contrast, not a condition.
 
• "**Whereas**" (Option 4) is incorrect as it is used to show contrast between two clauses, not a condition.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"He will be promoted **provided that**__ he improves his communication and leadership skills."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Unless"** is used for negative conditions, e.g., "You will fail unless you study."
 
• **Option 2: "Although"** is used to indicate contrast, e.g., "Although it was raining, they went outside."
 
• **Option 4: "Whereas"** is used to compare two contrasting ideas, e.g., "He enjoys swimming, whereas she prefers running."
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The children said, "Teacher! Please show us what is inside the box."

options.text: The children requested the teacher to show them what was inside the box.
The children urged the teacher to show us what was inside the box.
The children requested the teacher to show them what has been inside the box.
The children requested the teacher please show them what was inside the box.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech Conversion:** The process of converting direct speech to indirect speech involves changes in pronouns, verb tenses, and sentence structure while maintaining the original meaning.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun "us" becomes "them":** In indirect speech, the pronoun changes to match the perspective of the reporting speaker.
 
• **Verb tense change:** "is" (present tense) changes to "was" (past tense) to align with the rules of reported speech.
 
• **Request structure:** The direct request "Please show us" is converted to "requested the teacher to show them" to appropriately convey the polite request in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The quotation marks and direct speech format are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The reporting verb "requested" is followed by the infinitive form "to show" for a polite request.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The children requested the teacher to show them what was inside the box.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** The children urged the teacher to show us what was inside the box.
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun "us" instead of "them" for indirect speech.
 
• The word "urged" is inappropriate as it suggests forcefulness, whereas the tone of the sentence is a polite request.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The children requested the teacher to show them what has been inside the box.
 
 
• Incorrect verb tense: "has been" (present perfect) does not match the past tense "was" required in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The children requested the teacher please show them what was inside the box.
 
 
• Incorrect structure: "please show" retains direct speech format, which is not used in indirect speech.
 
 
</ul

Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

__**Five kilometres are the distance **__between my house and the airport.

options.text: Five kilometre is to be the distance

__
 
• In English grammar, measurements, distances, and quantities are usually treated as singular subjects, even if they appear in plural form (e.g., five kilometres).
 
• The verb "**is**" is the correct singular form to agree with the subject "**Five kilometres**" in this context.
 
• **Option 1** and **Option 4** are incorrect because the plural verb "**are**" is not grammatically correct for this usage.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because "**is to be the distance**" is not a natural or standard construction in English.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The government has announced a new policy.

options.text: A new policy has been announced by the government.
A new policy was announced by the government.
A new policy had been announced by the government.
A new policy is being announced by the government.

questions.solution:

__ 
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The government has announced a new policy." 
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a new policy" at the beginning. 
 
• Change the active verb form "has announced" to "has been announced" (present perfect passive). 
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the government." 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"A new policy has been announced by the government."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 4: **"A new policy is being announced by the government." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

My friend told me that she could not come.

options.text: My friend said to me, "She could not come."
My friend said to me, "I can not come."
My friend said to me, "I could not come."
My friend said to me, "I might not come."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** My friend told me that she could not come.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"She could not come" becomes "I can not come" in direct speech:**
 
 
• The pronoun "she" is converted to "I" because the speaker (my friend) is referring to herself in direct speech.
 
• The modal verb "could" in indirect speech is the back-shifted form of "can"; therefore, the direct speech uses "can" when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The indirect reporting verb "told" is converted to "said to" in direct speech.
 
• The preposition "to me" is retained to indicate the listener.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The sentence starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a full stop inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My friend said to me, 'I can not come.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "My friend said to me, 'She could not come.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because the pronoun "she" in direct speech does not align with the speaker (my friend).
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "My friend said to me, 'I could not come.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because "could" remains "could" in indirect speech only if it was already "could" or "can" is being back-shifted; however, to form the indirect "could", the direct form typically uses "can" to denote ability.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "My friend said to me, 'I might not come.'" 
 
 
• Incorrect because "might not" implies possibility, whereas "could not" conveys inability.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The clause "wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates" is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Defining an Adjective Clause.***

 
 
• An **Adjective Clause** (also known as a relative clause) is a dependent clause that modifies a noun or pronoun. It typically starts with relative pronouns like *who, which, that* or relative adverbs like *where, when, **wherein***.
 
• In the sentence: "These imposts embody the principle of progressive taxation, **wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates**...", the clause starting with "wherein" provides more information about the noun phrase **"progressive taxation."**
 
 
 
• ***The Role of "Wherein".***
 
 
• The word "wherein" acts as a relative adverb meaning "in which." Since it describes the specific nature of the "progressive taxation" mentioned just before it, it functions exactly like an adjective.
 
 
 
• ***Eliminating Other Options.***
 
 
• **Option 1**: It does not explain "why" (cause) the taxation exists; it describes what it is.
 
• **Option 3**: It does not act as a subject or object (Noun Clause); it is a modifier.
 
• **Option 4**: While "wherein" can feel related to "where," in this context, it isn't describing a physical location (place), but rather a conceptual principle.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tax terminology often uses formal relative adverbs like **wherein**, **whereby**, or **whereof** to connect legal principles to their specific applications. These almost always form **Adjective Clauses**.

questions.question:
Rewrite the following sentence by converting it to Interrogative Negative sentence:

"India imposes ancillary duties such as customs duty on imports, intended both to generate revenue and to protect domestic industries."

options.text: Does India impose ancillary duties, such as customs duty, on imports with the intention of both generating revenue and protecting domestic industries?
Why India impose ancillary duties, such as customs duty, on imports with the intention of both generating revenue and protecting domestic industries?
Doesn't India impose ancillary duties, such as customs duty, on imports with the intention of both generating revenue and protecting domestic industries?
Did India impose ancillary duties, such as customs duty, on imports with the intention of both generating revenue and protecting domestic industries?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Understanding the Interrogative Negative.***

 
 
• An **Interrogative Negative** sentence is a question that also contains a negation (not). It is often used to confirm a fact that the speaker believes to be true or to express surprise.
 
• The original sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** ("India imposes..."). To form a question in this tense, we use the auxiliary verb **do** or **does**. Since "India" is a singular subject, we use **does**.
 
 
 
• ***Structure of the Transformation.***
 
 
• The standard formula for an interrogative negative sentence is: **Auxiliary Verb + Subject + Not + Main Verb...?** or the contracted form: **Auxiliary Verb-n't + Subject + Main Verb...?**
 
• Original: *India imposes...*
 
• Interrogative Negative: ***Doesn't** India **impose**...?* (Note that when using 'does', the main verb 'imposes' loses its '-s' and returns to its base form 'impose').
 
 
 
• ***Evaluating the Options.***
 
 
• **Option 1**: This is a simple Interrogative sentence (positive question), not negative.
 
• **Option 2**: This is a 'Wh-' question and is grammatically incorrect (missing the auxiliary 'does').
 
• **Option 4**: This is in the **Past Tense** ("Did"), whereas the original sentence is in the Present Tense.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When transforming sentences, always ensure the tense remains consistent. If the original statement uses "imposes" (Present), your question must use "does" or "doesn't" (Present).

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the primary structural change introduced by GST?

options.text: It created a single tax replacing many indirect taxes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: It created a single tax replacing many indirect taxes.***

 
 
• This is the **primary structural change** mentioned. The passage states that the GST "subsumed a plethora of erstwhile levies such as excise duty, service tax, and value-added tax," effectively creating a "unified national market."
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: It reduced income tax rates.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage categorizes income tax as a "direct tax." GST is an indirect tax, and the text does not mention any changes to income tax rates.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It eliminated customs duties.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly mentions that India "imposes ancillary duties such as customs duty on imports" in addition to the GST regime.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It increased corporate tax rates.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Corporate tax is listed as a direct tax; the passage does not state that GST led to an increase in corporate tax rates.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Taxes**: The passage distinguishes between direct taxes (paid by individuals/entities on earnings) and indirect taxes (borne by consumers on goods/services).

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P. A hiss of air and a flat tire ended his road trip suddenly.

Q. He raised the car, his wrench already loosening lug nuts with a squeak.

R. With a grunt, he replaced the worn tire with the tiny spare, a stopgap measure.

S. A few minutes later, the vehicle was back on the road, ready to proceed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence sequence should be logically structured to describe the events in the order they happen.
 
• **Sentence P** is the first sentence because it introduces the event of the flat tire, which sets the context for the subsequent actions:
 
 
• "A hiss of air and a flat tire ended his road trip suddenly."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q** follows next as it describes the immediate action taken to address the flat tire:
 
 
• "He raised the car, his wrench already loosening lug nuts with a squeak."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R** comes third because it details how the flat tire was replaced with a spare tire:
 
 
• "With a grunt, he replaced the worn tire with the tiny spare, a stopgap measure."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S** is the final sentence as it concludes the sequence with the car being back on the road:
 
 
• "A few minutes later, the vehicle was back on the road, ready to proceed."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **P, Q, R, S**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"A hiss of air and a flat tire ended his road trip suddenly. He raised the car, his wrench already loosening lug nuts with a squeak. With a grunt, he replaced the worn tire with the tiny spare, a stopgap measure. A few minutes later, the vehicle was back on the road, ready to proceed."</div

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of homophones can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

"His years of effort came to ________ when the invention was rejected, but he reminded himself that failure does ________ define a person."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. naught, not**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"naught"** means "nothing" or "zero." It is often used to describe situations where efforts or results lead to no outcome or significance. (कुछ नहीं / शून्य)
 
 
• **Example:** All their hard work came to naught when the project was canceled.
 
 

 
• The word **"not"** is used as a negative particle to indicate refusal, denial, or negation of a statement. (नहीं)
 
 
• **Example:** Failure does not define a person; perseverance does.
 
 

 
• In the given sentence, "naught" fits the first blank as it implies that the years of effort led to nothing, and "not" fits the second blank to negate the idea that failure defines a person.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. naught, not**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: naught, nought** (शून्य, शून्य)
 
 
• "Naught" means "nothing" or "zero," as explained earlier.
 
• "Nought" also means "zero" or "nothing," but it is primarily used in British English for numerical references.
 
• **Example:** The score was nought to ten in the football match.
 
• This option does not fit the second blank because "nought" is not suitable for negation.
 
 

 
• **Option 2: not, naught** (नहीं, शून्य)
 
 
• "Not" is used for negation, as explained earlier.
 
• "Naught" means "nothing" or "zero."
 
• This option places "not" in the first blank, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: not, nought** (नहीं, शून्य)
 
 
• "Not" is used for negation, as explained earlier.
 
• "Nought" is used for numerical zero or nothing.
 
• This option does not fit because "nought" is not appropriate for the context of the first blank.
